page: Microsoft Azure E96s_v7 is a memory-optimized instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz across an x86_64 architecture. The server provides 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor architecture includes 480 MB of shared L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 48 KB of L1d cache, supplemented by hardware instruction sets including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography engines (AES, VAES, SHA-NI). System memory totals 768.0 GB, yielding an 8.0 GB-per-vCPU ratio. The instance features no local storage and does not include hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and high-throughput memory processing. The multi-core stress-ng metric reaches 102,250.79 points, while the PassMark CPU score ranks in the top tier at 109,110.34, buoyed by high vector and matrix performance in extended instructions (127,838.02) and CPU encryption (107,455.51). In contrast, single-thread performance is modest, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2,248.08 within the average tier. Memory bandwidth achieves top-tier throughput in cached reads at 7,543.56 GB/sec, while large uncached reads and writes register at 349.82 GB/sec and 134.51 GB/sec, respectively.

In operational benchmarks, the instance delivers top-tier results in Redis SET operations (160.72 million operations/sec), PassMark database operations (33,095.51), and static web throughput (151.85 GB/sec). Compression workloads demonstrate high throughput, reaching 604.05 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and 36.46 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. CPU-based LLM inference yields top-tier prompt processing speeds across various model weights, such as 311.71 tokens/sec on 7B models and 40.01 tokens/sec on 70B models, though autoregressive token generation rates settle into middle and strong tiers due to memory-bound execution limits.

The absence of integrated local NVMe disks requires external network-attached storage for persistent and temporary data, which introduces external storage architectural considerations. Resource density favors workloads that require substantial in-memory capacity paired with high concurrent core counts. The E96s_v7 is well aligned for large in-memory databases, Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency web tiers, relational database engines, and CPU-based matrix inference pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96s_v7 is a memory-optimized server powered by a 4.2 GHz Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) and 768.0 GB of RAM. Designed on the x86_64 architecture with a generous 480 MB L3 cache, it incorporates AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. The configuration lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote storage volumes. Across benchmarks, it shows exceptional multi-core throughput, reflected in a PassMark CPU score of 109,110.34 and Redis throughput exceeding 160 million operations per second. While single-thread compute ranks in the average tier, its cached read bandwidth reaches 7,543.56 GB/sec and database operations reach the top tier. These characteristics position the instance for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including large-scale Redis deployments, relational databases, data compression pipelines, and CPU-driven matrix inference.
